name: Goddess Pose
hero_alt: Goddess Pose, seen from the front
meta_description: Shallow squat, knees caving in, torso leaning, arms straightening? Four things usually hold back Goddess Pose, and a daily exercise that fixes each one.
og_description: Four things usually hold back Goddess Pose, and a daily exercise that fixes each one.
lede: Wide stance, toes turned out, hips low, knees over toes, torso tall, arms in a goalpost. Here’s the rubric Posewise measures it against, and what to train when you miss.
rubric_intro: Posewise checks six things from the front. Here’s what good looks like.

rubric.name: Knees
rubric.good: Tracking out over your toes, not caving in

rubric.name: Elbows
rubric.good: Bent to a right angle, like a goalpost

rubric.name: Shoulders
rubric.good: Level, both elbows at the same height

fixes.action: Build leg strength and open your inner thighs
fixes.outcome: you’ll sink deeper into the squat.
fixes.why: Depth usually stops where leg strength runs out. Tight inner thighs can cap it too.
fixes.cue: Sink your hips lower, knees over your toes.

fixes.outcome: your knees will track out over your toes.
fixes.why: When the outer glutes are weak, the knees cave in toward the big toes.
fixes.cue: Press your knees outward, in line with your toes.

fixes.outcome: your torso will stay tall over your hips.
fixes.why: When the trunk tires, the chest tips forward and the pose turns into an ordinary squat.
fixes.cue: Lift your chest and stack your torso over your hips.

fixes.outcome: your arms will settle into the cactus shape.
fixes.why: Straightening or uneven arms usually point to shoulders running out of rotation, so one side gives first.
fixes.cue: Elbows at shoulder height, bent to a right angle.

cues: And one cue: turn your toes out about 45°, so your knees can point the same way.

faq.q: How low should I squat in Goddess Pose?
faq.a: Aim for thighs close to parallel with the floor, but only as low as your knees can stay over your toes. A higher squat with good knees beats a deep one with knees caving in.

faq.q: How far should my toes turn out in Goddess Pose?
faq.a: About 45°, with your heels in and toes out. Your knees should point the same direction as your toes.

faq.q: Why do my knees cave in during Goddess Pose?
faq.a: Usually weak outer hips, or toes turned out further than your hips allow. Press your knees out toward your little toes.

faq.q: What do I do with my arms in Goddess Pose?
faq.a: The common version is cactus arms: elbows at shoulder height, bent to about 90°, palms forward. Hands at your heart works too.

faq.q: How can I check my Goddess Pose form at home?
faq.a: Film yourself from the front. Or use Posewise, an iPhone app that measures your Goddess Pose with the camera, speaks corrections as you hold it, and builds a six-minute daily plan for what it finds.

llms_summary: the four things that usually hold back Goddess Pose (leg strength for squat depth, outer-hip strength for knee tracking, core strength for an upright torso, shoulder mobility for even cactus arms), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
